the highest level of daily nutrient intake that is unlikely to 
have any adverse health effects on almost all individuals in the 
general population. The DRIs for the macronutrients, vitamins, 
and minerals, including the ULs, are presented on the inside 
front and back covers and opening page of this text. The 
AMDRs are ranges of intakes of macronutrients associated with 
reduced risk of chronic disease. The AMDRs for fat, carbohy-
drate, and protein are based on energy intake by age group. See 
Table 11-1 and the DRI tables on the inside front and back covers 
of this text.
Target Population
Each of the nutrient recommendation categories in the DRI sys-
tem is used for specific purposes among individuals or popula-
tions. As noted previously, the EAR is used for evaluating the 
nutrient intake of populations. The AI and RDA can be used for 
individuals. Nutrient intakes between the RDA and the UL may 
further define intakes that may promote health or prevent disease 
in the individual.
Age and Gender Groups
Because nutrient needs are highly individualized depending on 
age, gender, and the reproductive status of females, the DRI 
framework has 10 age groupings, including age group catego-
ries for children, adolescents, men and women 51 to 70 years of 
age, and those older than 70 years of age. It separates three 
age group categories each for pregnancy and lactation—14 to 
18 years, 19 to 30 years, and 31 to 50 years of age.
